programs.name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
programs.host: MIT / Center for Excellence in Education
programs.desc: The most prestigious STEM summer program in the US. 100 rising seniors conduct original research mentored by MIT scientists in labs across Boston. ~3,000 applicants, ~100 admitted (~3%). Covers the full research cycle: coursework, lab work, and a formal conference-style presentation. Fully free — tuition, housing, meals all covered.
programs.note: Applications for RSI 2027 open in October 2026 and close in early-to-mid December 2026 (typically the Wednesday of the second full week). Late applications are never considered.

history.note: Applications for 2026 are closed (deadline was Dec 10, 2025). Applications for RSI 2027 typically open in October 2026 at cee.org.

programs.name: MITES Summer
programs.desc: Rigorous 6-week residential program for rising seniors passionate about STEM. Acceptance rate 1.5–4% — among the most selective HS programs in the US. Five college-level courses in math, life sciences, physics, engineering, and a project elective. Prioritizes underrepresented students but all US citizens/permanent residents may apply. All costs covered.
programs.note: MITES runs a common application across MITES Summer, MITES Semester and MOSTEC. The deadline has held at February 1 for several cycles; recommendations are due about two weeks later.

history.note: Applications for 2026 are closed (deadline Feb 2). Apply in fall of junior year for 2027 — same application as MITES Semester.

programs.desc: One of the most prestigious math programs in the world. ~75 students spend 6 weeks exploring deep number theory and proof-based mathematics as practicing mathematicians. Application requires solving a rigorous problem set. Must have completed 9th grade and be at least 14. Free for families earning under $80k.
programs.note: 2027 application is closed. Applications for PROMYS 2028 open in January 2028 at promys.org.

history.note: 2026 application is closed. Applications for PROMYS 2027 open in January 2027 at promys.org.

programs.name: Ross Mathematics Program
programs.desc: One of the oldest and most respected number-theory immersion programs in the world, running since 1957. Students spend six weeks on a single deep problem set exploring the integers from first principles — the motto is 'think deeply of simple things.' No lectures-and-homework rhythm: you build the mathematics yourself with counselor guidance. Alumni populate math faculties worldwide.
programs.note: Applications typically open in early January and close at the end of March. Expect to spend serious time on the entrance problem set — it is the core of the application.

programs.name: Boston University RISE
programs.dates: Six weeks, late June – early August 2027
programs.desc: Research in Science & Engineering places rising seniors in a BU lab for six weeks under a graduate-student or postdoc mentor, working on a genuine research question. Choose the Internship track (lab placement) or the Practicum track (group project in computational neurobiology or similar). Ends with a poster symposium.
programs.note: The internship track is substantially more competitive than the practicum. Financial aid is real but limited — apply early if you need it.

programs.name: Jackson Laboratory Summer Student Program
programs.desc: Ten weeks of independent genetics and genomics research at one of the world's leading mammalian-genetics institutes, on the coast of Maine next to Acadia National Park. Students are paired with a JAX faculty mentor, design their own project, and present at a closing symposium. Housing, meals and travel are covered and students receive a stipend.
programs.note: Extremely competitive — a few dozen places against well over a thousand applicants. Free, paid, and residential, which is a rare combination.

programs.name: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
programs.desc: Paid biomedical research internships in NIH's intramural labs — the largest biomedical research enterprise in the world. High school students work alongside principal investigators on real projects across immunology, neuroscience, cancer biology, bioinformatics and more. Must be 17 by the program start date and a US citizen or permanent resident.
programs.note: Applying is only half the job — you must also email individual investigators whose work interests you. Applicants who contact PIs directly are far more likely to be placed.

programs.name: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program
programs.desc: Seven weeks of hands-on laboratory research at a Nobel-laureate-dense biomedical institute on Manhattan's Upper East Side. Students join a working lab, are mentored by a scientist, and present their findings at a final symposium. Includes a stipend. Strongly oriented toward New York-area students.
programs.note: Applications generally open in December and close in early January — one of the earliest deadlines in the cycle. Don't wait for spring.

programs.name: MSK HOPP Summer Student Program
programs.desc: The Human Oncology and Pathogenesis Program places high school students in cancer-research labs at MSK for a full eight-week summer. Students are assigned a mentor, run a project, attend a lecture series on cancer biology, and present a poster at the end. Paid.
programs.note: You must be 18 by the program start date for most lab placements — check the current eligibility rules before investing time in the application.

programs.name: Princeton Summer Journalism Program
programs.dates: Ten-day residency, August 2027, plus a year-long college-admissions component
programs.desc: A free, all-expenses-paid journalism intensive for low-income high school juniors. Students report and publish a real newspaper, meet working journalists from national outlets, and then receive a full year of free college-admissions counselling afterwards. Travel, housing and meals are all covered.
programs.note: Strict income eligibility (household income near or below the federal median). The year-long admissions counselling afterwards is arguably worth more than the ten days themselves.

programs.name: MIT MOSTEC
programs.dates: June 2027 – February 2028 (online, with a campus conference)
programs.desc: MIT Online Science, Technology and Engineering Community — a free six-month online program for rising seniors from underrepresented or underserved backgrounds. Two science-and-engineering courses, a science-writing course, mentoring, and a fully funded trip to MIT for a closing conference. Runs from the summer through the following winter.
programs.note: Shares the single MITES common application with MITES Summer and MITES Semester — one form, three programs, ranked by preference.

programs.name: Perimeter Institute ISSYP
programs.desc: The International Summer School for Young Physicists brings students to Perimeter Institute for two weeks of quantum mechanics, general relativity, cosmology and particle physics taught by working theoretical physicists. Runs both a virtual cohort and a smaller in-person cohort. Tuition, accommodation and meals are free for the in-person school.
programs.note: Open to students worldwide. The virtual edition takes many more students than the in-person one — apply to both if eligible.

programs.name: Iowa Young Writers' Studio
programs.desc: The high school arm of the Iowa Writers' Workshop, the most storied creative-writing program in America. Two weeks of daily workshop in fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, playwriting or TV writing, taught by Iowa MFA writers. Admission is by writing sample.
programs.note: Admission is purely on the strength of the writing sample — grades and test scores are not considered. A shorter online session also runs each summer.

programs.name: Kenyon Review Young Writers Workshop
programs.desc: Two weeks of intensive generative writing run by The Kenyon Review, one of the country's leading literary magazines. Small workshops, twice-daily writing sessions, no grades, no genre requirements. Focused on generating new work rather than polishing a portfolio.
programs.note: Admission is rolling and sessions fill early — applying in January or February is meaningfully better than waiting for spring.

programs.name: Notre Dame Leadership Seminars
programs.desc: A fully funded two-week seminar for about 100 rising seniors, built around discussion-based courses on questions of ethics, justice and human dignity. Tuition, housing and meals are covered by Notre Dame; students pay only travel. Highly selective and academically demanding.
programs.note: One of very few genuinely free humanities-oriented pre-college programs at a major university.

programs.name: UC Santa Cruz Science Internship Program (SIP)
programs.desc: Ten weeks of authentic research on a UCSC team led by a graduate student or postdoc, across astronomy, genomics, engineering, ecology, physics and more. Students contribute to an ongoing project rather than a manufactured exercise, and many go on to co-author posters or papers. Both residential and remote placements.
programs.note: One of the larger authentic-research programs by cohort size, which makes it meaningfully less of a lottery than the tiny lab programs.

programs.name: Naval Academy Summer STEM Program
programs.desc: A one-week residential STEM immersion on the Naval Academy's Annapolis campus — robotics, cyber, naval architecture, propulsion and materials, taught in USNA labs by academy faculty and midshipmen. Separate rising-9th, -10th and -11th grade sessions with age-appropriate curricula.
programs.note: Cheap for what it is, and no service obligation. Attending does not commit you to a military path but does signal genuine interest if you later apply to a service academy.

programs.name: West Point Summer Leaders Experience
programs.host: United States Military Academy at West Point
programs.desc: A one-week look at cadet life for rising seniors seriously considering West Point: academic workshops, military training, physical fitness testing, and living in the barracks. Participation is a documented data point in the West Point admissions file.
programs.note: Effectively part of the West Point admissions funnel. Applications open in January and the cohort fills before the stated deadline.

programs.name: SPARC
programs.host: Summer Program on Applied Rationality and Cognition
programs.desc: A free two-week program in quantitative reasoning, probability, decision theory, game theory and cognitive science for mathematically strong high schoolers. Draws heavily from the olympiad and competition-math community. Instructors come from research, quantitative finance and AI labs.
programs.note: Free including room and board. The application is unusual — expect puzzles and reasoning problems rather than a conventional essay-and-transcript package.

programs.name: Stanford AI4ALL
programs.cost: Sliding scale, free for many admitted students
programs.desc: The original AI4ALL site, founded at Stanford's AI Lab to bring students underrepresented in AI into the field early. Three weeks of AI fundamentals plus a research project with a Stanford faculty mentor on applications like computational biology, robotics or NLP. Tuition is means-tested and many students attend free.
programs.note: Aimed at 9th and 10th graders specifically — one of the few strong research-adjacent options for younger students.

programs.name: Carleton Summer Liberal Arts Institute
programs.desc: A fully funded three-week seminar for rising seniors, taught by Carleton faculty in small discussion classes across humanities, social sciences and quantitative reasoning. Students pay only travel. Designed to show what a genuine liberal-arts classroom feels like.
programs.note: Free and small, which makes it competitive. A strong option for students who want humanities depth rather than another STEM camp.

programs.name: Kode With Klossy
programs.desc: Free two-week coding camps for girls, trans and non-binary students aged 13–18, in web development, mobile app development, machine learning and data science. Runs in cities across the US plus virtual sessions, with laptops provided where needed. Alumni get ongoing community and scholarship access.
programs.note: Genuinely free, including materials. Beginner-friendly — no prior programming experience required.

programs.name: Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program
programs.desc: A paid eight-week summer mentorship in fisheries and aquatic science, matching students with a professional biologist at a state agency, university or federal lab near where they live. Field work, sampling, tagging and data collection. Comes with a $3,000 stipend.
programs.note: Placements are local, so there is no housing or travel cost — one of the most accessible paid research experiences available to high schoolers.

programs.name: City of Hope Roberts Summer Student Academy
programs.desc: The Eugene and Ruth Roberts Summer Student Academy gives high schoolers a ten-week paid biomedical research placement at a major cancer and diabetes research centre outside Los Angeles. Students join a lab, run a project, and present at a closing symposium alongside undergraduate and graduate researchers.
programs.note: Must be 16 by the program start date. Longer than most high school lab programs, which means real ownership of a project.

programs.name: AwesomeMath Summer Program
programs.dates: Three weeks per session, June – July 2027
programs.desc: Three-week olympiad-math training sessions for students preparing for AMC, AIME, USAMO and similar competitions. Courses in number theory, combinatorics, algebra and geometry at several difficulty levels. Admission via a placement test rather than a competitive essay application.
programs.note: Admission is by placement test, so it is far less of a lottery than the free olympiad programs — a good fallback if Mathcamp or PROMYS don't work out.

programs.name: Barnard Pre-College Programs
programs.dates: One to four weeks, June – July 2027
programs.desc: Pre-college sessions for students who identify as women, on Barnard's Manhattan campus. Tracks include the four-week Liberal Arts Intensive, the Summer in the City exploration of New York institutions, and shorter STEM and writing intensives. Residential and commuter options.
programs.note: Admission is rolling rather than competitive — this is a pay-to-attend enrichment program, not a selective credential.

programs.name: National Student Leadership Conference
programs.dates: Six to nine days, June – July 2027
programs.desc: Career-exploration conferences on university campuses across the US, covering medicine, engineering, law, forensic science, international diplomacy, business and more. Simulation-heavy — mock trials, mock surgeries, mock UN sessions — rather than academic coursework. Expanding to the University of Oxford.
programs.note: Open enrolment: anyone who applies and pays attends. Useful for exploring a career interest, but it carries no admissions selectivity signal.

events.name: NASA Space Apps Challenge
events.desc: The world's largest hackathon with 55,000+ participants from 160+ countries. Use NASA's open data to solve Earth and space science challenges. Teams of 2–6. Local events in 100+ cities — find one near you at spaceappschallenge.org.

events.name: Hack Club Hackathons (100+)
events.desc: Hack Club maintains the definitive directory of 100+ high school hackathons across 30+ states and 26 countries. Most events are free and cover food. Find events at hackathons.hackclub.com — searchable by location and date.

events.name: HackMIT Blueprint
events.desc: MIT's flagship high school hackathon. Beginner-friendly tracks, workshops taught by MIT undergrads, and hands-on mentorship. Build a project in one weekend alongside 400+ students from across the country.

events.name: Major League Hacking (MLH)
events.desc: The official student hackathon league with 200+ sanctioned events per year, open to high schoolers. Company sponsors include Microsoft, GitHub, and Google. Each MLH event is a chance to meet recruiters and build your developer profile.

events.name: PennApps
events.desc: One of the oldest and most prestigious college hackathons in the US — open to high schoolers. Tracks in software, hardware, AI, and social good. 1,200+ attendees, mentors from top tech companies, and real recruiting connections.

events.name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
events.desc: The nation's most prestigious precollege science competition since 1942. Submit original research in any STEM field. 300 scholars selected nationally; 40 finalists travel to Washington, DC. One of the strongest differentiators for Ivy admissions.

events.name: Regeneron ISEF
events.desc: The world's largest international precollege STEM fair. 1,800+ students from 70+ countries present original research. Must qualify through a regional or state-affiliated fair first. Even regional ISEF qualification is a strong credential for college admissions.

events.name: USACO (USA Computing Olympiad)
events.desc: The top competitive programming competition for high schoolers. Monthly contests: Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum → USA IOI team. USACO Gold or Platinum is among the strongest CS credentials for any college application.

events.name: AMC 10/12 → AIME → USAMO
events.desc: The official pathway to the US Math Olympiad and the International Math Olympiad (IMO). AMC 10/12 → AIME → USAMO. AIME qualification is a solid credential; USAMO qualification is exceptional. Prepare using Art of Problem Solving.

events.name: WAICY — World AI Competition for Youth
events.desc: The world's largest AI competition for ages 13–18 with 3,000+ participants from 40+ countries. Tracks include AI project showcase, LLM applications, and AI creative work. Team-based format with mentor feedback rounds. Strong portfolio piece for CS and AI-focused students.

events.name: Kaggle Competitions
events.desc: The world's largest data science community. Open to high schoolers. Start with beginner challenges to build a track record. Even placing in the top 10% of a Kaggle competition is a meaningful CS portfolio piece.

events.name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
events.desc: Create a 3-minute original video explaining a complex scientific concept in a clear, creative way. Open globally to ages 13–18. One of the largest science prizes for young people. Past winners have explained quantum entanglement, CRISPR, and general relativity.

events.name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
events.desc: Recognizes students 18 and under who have completed a significant piece of original work in STEM, literature, music, or philosophy. Requires genuinely exceptional, publishable-quality research or creative work. Very few awarded each year.

events.name: JSHS — Junior Science & Humanities Symposium
events.desc: Students present original STEM research to panels of military scientists. Regional → national structure. Top finalists receive substantial scholarships and present at the national symposium. Covers all STEM disciplines. Underrated — competition is less intense than ISEF but highly prestigious.

events.name: Conrad Innovation Summit
events.desc: Teams solve real-world problems using STEM innovation and entrepreneurship, then pitch to NASA astronauts, engineers, and industry leaders at the annual summit. Categories include aerospace, energy, cybersecurity, and health sciences. Open globally to students ages 13–18.

events.name: MIT THINK Scholars Program
events.prize: $1,000 project budget + MIT mentorship + funded campus visit
events.desc: Unlike most science competitions, THINK funds projects that have NOT been built yet. Submit a detailed proposal for a science or engineering project, and if selected you get a budget, weekly mentorship from MIT students, and a trip to campus. Ideal for students with an idea but no lab or funding.

events.name: Congressional App Challenge
events.prize: Winning app displayed in the US Capitol
events.desc: Each participating member of Congress runs a district-level app competition, so you compete against students in your own district rather than nationally — dramatically better odds than national contests. Any platform, any language. Winners are recognised by their representative and their app is displayed in the Capitol.

events.name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
events.desc: One of the largest corporate scholarship programs in the US, awarding 150 scholarships of $20,000 each to graduating seniors on the basis of leadership and service rather than test scores. Roughly 100,000 applicants a year. Opens in August of senior year and closes in October.

events.name: Physics Olympiad (F=ma → USAPhO)
events.prize: US Physics Team training camp + international selection
events.desc: The US pathway to the International Physics Olympiad. Start with the F=ma exam in January — 25 mechanics questions in 75 minutes. Top scorers advance to USAPhO, then to the training camp at the University of Maryland, and finally five students represent the US internationally.

events.name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
events.dl: Register through your school by Jan 2027
events.prize: National Finals training camp + IBO team selection
events.desc: The US selection pathway for the International Biology Olympiad, run by the same organisation behind RSI. Roughly 10,000 students take the Open Exam, 500 advance to Semifinals, and 20 reach the National Finals residential training camp. Campbell Biology is the de facto syllabus.
